patch.value: Remove historical host paths and non-public Git identities before release approval

A fresh all-refs audit found no credential or private-key patterns, but two historical pmc-emom files contain an absolute host path in older Git commits and two distinct author/committer identities use non-public email domains. Current tracked files are clean. Because remediation requires a coordinated history rewrite, tag/ref verification, and downstream clone migration, publication remains blocked until a maintainer approves and executes the rewrite.

All refs and tags are rewritten or otherwise proven free of absolute private host paths; every author and committer identity is approved for public disclosure or rewritten to an approved noreply identity; signed/release tags and downstream clones are migrated without losing commits; a fresh all-refs credential, path, filename, and identity audit passes; maintainer explicitly approves publication after reviewing the rewrite evidence
Scan every revision from git rev-list --all for credential patterns and absolute host paths, then classify unique author and committer email domains without printing addresses.
No private host paths, credentials, or unapproved personal identities occur anywhere in reachable history.
Zero current-tree sensitive-pattern files and zero historical credentials/private keys; two historical PM paths contain an absolute host path and two Git identities use non-public domains.
Publishing or releasing before a coordinated rewrite could expose private host metadata or personal identity data.

patch.value: Pre-rewrite audit: 84 refs and 71 tags were enumerated; historical sensitive-filename matches are zero. One annotated tag exists, it is unsigned, and its tagger uses a non-public identity domain. Commit history has zero credential/private-key/LAN-IP matches, two PM paths retain an absolute host path in older revisions, and two author/committer identities use non-public domains. False-positive classification found no credential fixtures in this focused pattern set. Rewrite, signature disposition, disposable-mirror equivalence, and downstream fresh-clone migration validation remain intentionally pending maintainer approval.

1. Enumerate every ref and tag, then scan all reachable commit blobs for credential, private-key, absolute-host-path, and LAN-address patterns without printing secret values. 2. Enumerate historical filenames across all refs for env, key, credential, secret, and token artifacts. 3. Classify every author, committer, annotated-tag tagger, and signature identity against the approved public-domain allowlist. 4. Record annotated and signed tag inventories before rewriting. 5. Classify each content and filename match as a confirmed finding or documented synthetic false positive. 6. In a disposable mirror, rewrite approved identities and host paths, verify every ref, commit, tree, tag target, signature disposition, and PM history chain, then compare object/ref inventories. 7. Re-clone the rewritten repository and validate package gates plus documented downstream-clone migration instructions before any force update. 8. Repeat the complete scan after migration and obtain explicit maintainer publication approval.
